# Substrate notes and the worked ground-block case

Moved here from `SKILL.md` on 2026-08-01 to bring the body under the ~19,900-
character surviving prefix. Two of the three are substrate-conditional — they
bind only on particular surfaces — and the third is a worked case rather than a
rule. Nothing was cut.

## Substrate note — where the filer's-pen rules are satisfied structurally

From § *Step 0 — File the claim*.

Where the candidate is an engine-addressed object and the engine copies its bytes
(the substrate the originating program ran on), the retype step the filing rules
guard does not exist — so on that substrate the filer's-pen rules are satisfied
structurally, and only the composer-*packaging* rules (leakage, filing direction,
curation tilt) survive into the run.

**The full discipline binds any surface that reintroduces a retype step**: loose
prose, a pasted corpus, a REPL rendered to text (`PROGRAM_CONTEXT.md` §6.1;
`JUDGE_INTAKE_DESIGN.md` §1.2, both mirrored here).

## Substrate note — the record layer and model prose

From § *Step 5 — Execute in clean contexts*.

At the session layer a short rationale citing the deciding span aids the human
read. The engine of the originating program kept the record minimal — the model
supplied only `{verdict, drawback, abstainReason}` (`judge_spawn.ts`), no
rationale byte — and provided explainability through an engine **read-time
render** over those stored fields (`judge_explain.ts`;
`JUDGE_CONVOCATION_DESIGN.md` §13, mirrored here), so model prose never entered a
record. A deciding-span *address* was a deferred follow-on (that record's Option
B). The two layers align as far as the code-mediated pillar allows.

That engine is not required to run this skill, and its repository is deprecated.
The transferable rule is the one the arrangement served: **keep model prose out of
the stored record, and render explanations at read time over typed fields.**

## The worked case behind "the ground block carries relevant context only"

From § *Step 5*. This is the failure that bought the rule.

A ceremony spawned four seats over work its own composer had authored, and handed
one the exact probe by which it had already obtained a pre-registered finding.
The seat found it, and the audit seat ruled the run's independence
**unestablishable** — the composer *"had already run the probe, saw the result,
wrote it down as a prediction, then handed the probe to the seat."*

Three seats carried composer-stated facts while the composer's disclosure said
"three seats" and named two.

Separate pre-registration, clean contexts, and an audit seat were all in place, so
**no artifact discharges this; the ground blocks do.**

The re-run dispatched seven reviewers whose ground blocks carried the facts and
stated in as many words that no prediction was offered and none was wanted. They
returned findings the composer had not anticipated, several against the
composer's own work.
